watch_items.text: Whether any right-leaning outlet ever covers the Nevada fake-electors dismissal or the Miller/Moreno false-statements-to-court allegations
Whether the Delaney Hall ICE facility (now three deaths) draws a congressional or DHS response, and whether right-leaning outlets engage once a political angle emerges
Appeals in the NFA suppressor ruling and the Mamdani luxury-tax stay — both are early-stage and likely contested further
Whether Khanna's 2028 signaling and Pelosi's move against Wiener get synthesized into one 'Democratic Party direction' story, and any public response from Pelosi or Wiener
The denaturalization task force, birth-tourism task force, and 175,000 visa revocations — watch for any outlet linking these into one citizenship-policy narrative, and for legal challenges

Status of Alito's $2.9M fossil-fuel disclosure and the Fauci contempt referral — both silent multiple cycles now; distinct from today's new 'Fauci, Covid Vaccines and Miscarriages' right-only story, which should not be conflated with the contempt-referral thread

top_cluster.headline: A Guatemalan immigrant, Jose Chajon-Raxon, died following a medical emergency while detained at the Delaney Hall ICE facility in Newark, New Jersey, becoming the third detainee death at that facility.
top_cluster.left_framing: The Guardian centers the death within a broader indictment of the Trump administration's expanded immigration detention system, emphasizing a pattern of fatal failures, distrust of the official DHS explanation, and unanswered accountability questions. Mother Jones does not cover this story at all, instead focusing on alleged voter suppression of nursing home residents.
top_cluster.center_framing: The Hill reports the death straightforwardly as part of a developing pattern of deaths at the facility, raising accountability and medical-care-quality questions without strong ideological framing.
top_cluster.right_framing: No right-leaning outlet in this set covered the Delaney Hall detainee death. Fox News instead covered an unrelated story on detransitioners and alleged financial incentives in pediatric gender-transition care, meaning there is no right-of-center framing of this event to compare.
top_cluster.left_omissions: N/A for direct comparison — no right-leaning outlet in this set covered the story, so there is no right-side reporting for the left to be omitting.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right-leaning coverage (Fox News) omits the Delaney Hall detainee deaths entirely, covering an unrelated topic instead. This means any DHS/ICE response, defense of detention conditions, or context on detainee health screening that a right-leaning outlet might have offered is absent from this dataset.

blindspot_narrative: Right-leaning outlets are systematically avoiding stories where state or administration action produces sympathy for people the administration has targeted (ICE detainee deaths, the Nevada electors dismissal, Israeli settler violence, domestic-violence allegations against a GOP congressman), while left-leaning outlets are avoiding stories where courts or agencies hand the administration clean enforcement/deregulation wins (the suppressor ruling, birth-tourism task force, mass visa revocations). This isn't factual distortion so much as curated omission — each side appears to be maintaining a coherent 'state failure' or 'state competence' narrative by leaving out whatever complicates it.
